name: Signer
summary: Represents the authenticated caller of a transaction in Aptos Move.
securityNote: Always authenticate caller addresses using signer::address_of(caller) to prevent unauthorized access.

name: Capability Pattern
summary: A Move resource that grants exclusive authority to perform privileged actions.
securityNote: Never expose capabilities via public non-entry functions, otherwise any module can acquire them.

name: Resource
summary: A struct with the `key` ability that exists in global storage under an account address.
codeExample: struct Treasury has key { balance: u64 }
securityNote: Resources cannot be silently discarded or duplicated, preventing asset loss bugs common in other chains.

name: Abilities (copy, drop, store, key)
summary: Type gates controlling whether a value can be copied, dropped, stored in global storage, or used as a key.
codeExample: struct Coin has store { value: u64 }
securityNote: Giving `drop` or `copy` to value-bearing tokens allows accidental destruction or unauthorized inflation.

name: Acquires Annotation
summary: Explicit function annotation declaring which global resources are read or mutated.
securityNote: Move compiler enforces acquires declarations statically to prevent reentrancy and data race issues.

name: Entry Function
summary: Functions that can be invoked directly as a transaction payload by external accounts or wallets.
codeExample: public entry fun mint(account: &signer, amount: u64) { ... }
securityNote: Entry functions must validate all user inputs (zero amounts, unauthorized callers).

name: Fungible Asset Framework
summary: Aptos standard for digital commodities, tokens, and currencies using Object-based architecture.
securityNote: Leverage primary stores to avoid custom balance tracking bugs and ensure wallet compatibility.

name: Move Objects
summary: Aptos core primitive providing globally addressable, extensible containers for resources and capabilities.
securityNote: Manage DeleteRef and TransferRef carefully to prevent unwanted object transfers.
